To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fully cooperative local file caching outperforms two benchmark cases in terms of the utilities of different groups.

(1) we practically categorize MTs into different groups according to the heterogeneity of file preferences; (2) we formulate the problem as an optimization problem to maximize the utilities of different groups, where the maximum utility tradeoff of different groups are derived; (3) we show that the fully cooperative local cache is more effective than the partial cooperation and no cooperation, and the inter-group file sharing is more effective than no inter-group file sharing.

(1) The optimal caching distribution is the same under both fully cooperative and no-cooperation local caching; (2) The optimal caching distributions under the partial cooperation are between the fully cooperative and no cooperation cases; and (3) The optimal utility tradeoffs under the fully cooperative case are higher than that under the partial and no cooperation cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how to improve the performance of local caching by considering MTs’ heterogeneities in file preferences and the selfishness in their caching behaviors, which has not been studied in the existing works.

the cooperative local caching under heterogeneous file preferences and selfish behaviors, which can provide valuable guidelines for the practical deployment of cooperative local caching in the cellular communication systems.
the local caching problem in cellular systems with heterogeneous file preferences, which is practically important and has not been addressed before.

the fully cooperative caching is more beneficial to all groups of MTs compared with the two selfish cases, especially when the file size is small.

the fully cooperative local cache scheme outperforms the other schemes in terms of the overall file discovery probability, and the inter-group file sharing is beneficial for improving the overall utility.
the proposed local caching framework is effective in saving the network resources and reducing the download delay.

we have developed a novel framework of cooperative local caching under heterogeneous file preferences.
, in the fully cooperative local cache, we can obtain a Pareto-optimal utility tradeoff for all the groups, which is not achievable in either partial or no cooperation.
we propose a novel fully cooperative local caching scheme for heterogeneous file preferences and selfish behaviors of MTs.

, by considering MTs’ heterogeneous interests and selfish behaviors, the fully cooperative local file sharing can achieve the maximum utility tradeoff for different groups, which outperforms the benchmark cases.
